To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lateral variability in throughfall, root and soil respiration is large in mature oil palm, that sampling methods should take account of the pattern of variation, and that sampling density has a major influence on calculated means.
lateral tree-scale variability in mature oil palm plantation should be taken into consideration when scaling up from a single point sample.

(1) the spatial variability of throughfall, root mass and soil respiration is high in mature oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) plantations; (2) the sampling density needed for reliable estimates of these parameters depends on the type and strength of the spatial patterns; (3) the most appropriate sampling design for tree-scale parameters is a triangular grid; and (4) a triangular grid is also appropriate for sampling tree-scale parameters when the spatial patterns are unknown.
